s1.syndrome_frame: Acute flank pain with radiating abdominal pain and associated nausea
salient_findings: Sudden, dull left flank pain radiating to the lateral abdomen
Tenderness at the left costovertebral angle
Heterogenous left adrenal mass with local extension and invasion into surrounding structures
key_facts: Female patient in her mid-60s
Sudden onset of dull left flank pain
Pain radiates to the lateral abdomen
Nausea present
No exacerbating or alleviating factors noted
Family history of renal cell carcinoma
Medical history of hypertension, basal cell carcinoma, and an autoimmune condition
Long-term azathioprine and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim therapy
Previous episodes of unintentional weight loss, fever, polyarthralgia, and fatigue
Hemodynamically stable
Tenderness at the left costovertebral angle on physical examination
Laboratory results show mild anemia and elevated ESR
CT scan reveals a large heterogenous left adrenal mass with local extension and invasion

shortlist.label: Adrenal Cortical Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large heterogenous left adrenal mass with local extension and invasion on CT scan

shortlist.label: Adrenal Metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of basal cell carcinoma and presence of a large adrenal mass

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of dull left flank pain and presence of an adrenal mass

shortlist.label: Renal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of renal cell carcinoma and presence of a large abdominal mass

shortlist.label: Primary Adrenal Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of an autoimmune condition and presence of a large adrenal mass with lymph node involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of a large heterogenous left adrenal mass with local extension and invasion into surrounding structures, along with the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, is most consistent with adrenal cortical carcinoma. The family history of renal cell carcinoma, while notable, does not directly influence the diagnosis in this case, given the specific location and characteristics of the mass.

rejected.label: Adrenal Metastasis
rejected.why: While possible, the primary presentation and the large size of the adrenal mass suggest a primary adrenal tumor rather than a metastasis.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with symptoms related to excess catecholamine production, such as hypertension, tachycardia, and sweating, which are not prominently featured in this case.

rejected.label: Renal Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: The mass is specifically described as an adrenal mass, not renal, and the imaging findings do not suggest a primary renal tumor.

rejected.label: Primary Adrenal Lymphoma
rejected.why: Less common than other adrenal tumors and would typically present with more systemic symptoms of lymphoma, which are not described in this vignette.
